content.title: Controlled Inputs: State Owns the Value
content.hook: A text field has a value. That value could live mainly inside the browser input itself, or React can make state the source of truth.
goals: Build controlled inputs where React state is the source of truth for the current value and user input updates that state.

options.text: The browser changes the field, but React does not know anything happened.
The change handler reads `Ada`, state becomes `Ada`, and the input is rendered from that state.
React replaces the input with a button.
The input can no longer change.

feedback.correct: The controlled input keeps the value in the React state model.
feedback.incorrect: The controlled input keeps the value in the React state model.

content.title: Build it

options.text: The handler stores the old state instead of the new input value.
`value` should be removed because React cannot control inputs.

feedback.correct: The event provides the new text. The setter must receive that new value.
feedback.incorrect: The event provides the new text. The setter must receive that new value.

activities.title: State as a source of truth

content.title: State as a source of truth
content.text:
Why is this pattern useful? Because other UI can read the same state. ```jsx

Characters: {username.length}

``` Now the count and the input value come from the same fact.

content.title: Small extension

content.question: Which design has the clearest source of truth for the input value?

options.text: The DOM input and a separate state value that may disagree
React state, with the input rendered from that state
A variable created once outside the component

feedback.correct: A controlled input makes the state/value relationship explicit.
feedback.incorrect: A controlled input makes the state/value relationship explicit.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A controlled input is a small feedback loop: user input produces new state, and state produces the current input value.
**Senior habit:** When a form behaves strangely, ask where the value actually lives and whether there is more than one source of truth.
nextSteps: Build a controlled input and repair the handler so the state receives the new value from the event.
